rfi.title: The global machinery built to carry out Trump’s mass deportation drive
rfi.description: More than 25,000 people have been deported by the United States to countries other than their own since Donald Trump returned to power. As part of The Deportation Project, coordinated by Forbidden Stories – a Paris-based journalism network that pursues the work of reporters who have been threatened, jailed or killed – RFI is publishing investigations into how this policy operates, with their findings exposing a global system backed by hundreds of millions of dollars.

france24fr.description: 🇺🇳 Devant l’Assemblée générale de l’ONU, le président iranien Massoud #Pezeshkian a répondu aux propos du président américain de la veille, et affirmé mercredi que l’Iran avait été "victime du terrorisme", en référence à l’offensive menée par les États-Unis et Israël contre la République islamique.

france24fr.title: "L'Iran ne baissera jamais la tête" : le président iranien Pezeshkian défie les États-Unis
france24fr.description: Le président iranien, Massoud Pezeshkian, a accusé les États-Unis de "terrorisme" dans son discours face à l'Assemblée générale de l'ONU mercredi. Malgré la tonalité offensive de sa prise de parole, le dialogue a repris entre des responsables iraniens et l'émissaire américain Steve Witkoff en marge de la session de l'ONU.

observador.title: As notícias das 6h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Abraão: o que têm em comum Cristianismo, Islão e Judaísmo?
observador.description: Se as religiões monoteístas têm tanto em comum, a começar pela raiz em Abraão, porque é tão difícil a paz? Um episódio especial de "As Histórias da Bíblia" com respostas às perguntas dos ouvintes.

observador.title: A Glorieta de Tomás Ribeiro em Viseu
observador.description: Falamos ainda de melhoramentos introduzidos em Viseu pela sua Comissão de Iniciativa e Turismo; desta vez é o monumento comemorativo do 1º centenário do nascimento do poeta e estadista Tomás Ribeiro.

observador.title: Escultura, pintura, desenho e, só no fim, fotografia
observador.description:
Fotografia aparece na reta final do percurso e junta-se às restantes formas de
arte. Miguel Ruge fecha a visita à primeira de três exposições do ciclo Peter Meeker e
antecipa o que ainda está por vir.

observador.title: “É só um comprimido para dormir”: será mesmo inofensivo?
observador.description: Um comprimido pode ajudar a dormir, mas quando começa a tornar-se um problema? Quedas, alterações da memória e dependência são alguns dos riscos associados ao uso prolongado.

observador.title: Maus-tratos na escola: A professora, os gritos, as agressões
observador.description: Pais acusam uma professora de gritos, castigos e agressões a crianças. O Observador investigou o caso, os alertas feitos à escola e a resposta da direção.

observador.title: 4h. Enviado de Putin deverá viajar para os EUA
observador.description: Kirill Dmitriev deverá reunir com Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner à margem da Assembleia Geral da ONU. Ainda, contradições nos documentos da PJ entregues ao MP na queixa contra diretor Carlos Cabreiro.

observador.title: 3h. Contradições nos documentos da queixa a Carlos Cabreiro
observador.description: O Observador teve acesso à queixa de Aníbal Pinto e à documentação entregue ao Ministério Público. Ainda, enviado especial de Putin deverá viajar para os EUA para reunir com a administração Trump.

observador.title: 2h. Venezuela. Presidente interina promete eleições
observador.description: Delcy Rodríguez garante que instituições venezuelanas estão prontas para assegurar processo inclusivo e transparente. Ainda neste jornal, Zelensky pede à China ajuda para pôr fim à guerra na Ucrânia.

observador.title: 1h. EUA e China prolongam tréguas comerciais
observador.description: Anúncio do secretário do Tesouro norte-americano em entrevista à Fox News, pouco depois da chegada de Xi Jinping a território norte-americano. Ainda nesta edição, o último adeus a Jorge Palma.

observador.title: PS quer ir "além do PIB" para medir progresso
observador.description: A pouco mais de um mês dos Estados Gerais, Carneiro voltou a reunir Conselho Estratégico, desta vez para debater alternativas ao indicador mais batido para medir a prosperidade.

observador.title: Portugal assina memorando com países do Golfo
observador.description: Paulo Rangel assinou o acordo à margem da Assembleia Geral da ONU, em Nova Iorque. O memorando cria um novo quadro de consultas regulares entre Portugal e os países do Golfo.

observador.title: Palmas para Jorge no adeus ao mestre da Terra dos Sonhos
observador.description: À boleia do "fim do verão", Jorge Palma deixa um legado de música, luta e poesia. A despedida fez-se com família, amigos, fãs e nomes da política que não deixam esquecer a importância do artista.

observador.title: O mefistófeles tropical
observador.description: O que se passa no Brasil excede qualquer comparação. Pela escala e pela exibição de decadência do Supremo Tribunal Federal, o terceiro poder, que devia ser o garante e o árbitro dos outros dois.

observador.title: A matança dos inocentes
observador.description: Era uma vez uma pílula vermelha, uma pílula azul e um arco-íris monocromático

observador.title: 90 casas para 90 lugares
observador.description: Não é assistência social nem é sequer um prémio: é parte do preço que a cidade paga para conseguir contratar quem precisa.

observador.title: Da oscilação do preço do extremista
observador.description: Em 2026, a “ideologia” é uma patranha. Os supostos extremos não estão preocupados com ideologias, não têm visões de mundo nem modelos de sociedade diferentes para opor.

observador.title: 00h. Trump recebe Xi Jinping nos Estados Unidos
observador.description: O Presidente chinês não vai participar na Assembleia geral das Nações Unidas, em Nova Iorque. Ainda, esta quinta-feira, António José Seguro vai ser recebido pelo Papa no Vaticano.

spiegel.title: USA und China verlängern Waffenstillstand im Zollkrieg
spiegel.description: Seit mehr als einem Jahr bedrohen sich die USA und China gegenseitig mit hohen Zöllen. Jetzt soll der Handelskrieg abermals ein paar Monate ausgesetzt werden.

spiegel.title: Neustadt in Sachsen: 23 Verletzte nach Chemikalienvorfall bei Wohnmobilhersteller
spiegel.description: Weil offenbar Kältemittel aus einem Kühlschrank ausgetreten ist, kam es bei einem Hersteller von Reisemobilen in Sachsen zu einem Großeinsatz. Auch der Katastrophenschutz war vor Ort.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Russland greift mit ballistischen Raketen an – Tote in Kyjiw
spiegel.description: Raketenfragmente treffen eine Entbindungsklinik, in einem Wohnhaus werden Menschen unter den Trümmern vermutet. Selenskyj fordert mehr Abfangraketen, und ausgerechnet die Slowakei kritisiert Moskau scharf.

spiegel.title: Autohersteller haben im Sommer mehr Autos verkauft
spiegel.description: Die Nachfrage nach Autos hat seit Jahresbeginn wieder zugenommen. Profitiert haben davon vor allem die chinesischen Hersteller. Die deutschen Hersteller haben das Nachsehen.

spiegel.title: Roboter »Raibo2« lief in Südkorea Marathon unter viereinhalb Stunden
spiegel.description: Mit einer Ladung Strom und einer für Hobbyläufer passablen Zeit: Forscher in Südkorea haben einen vierbeinigen Roboter einen Marathon rennen lassen. Sie haben bereits eine Idee, wie sie »Raibo2« einsetzen könnten.

spiegel.title: Tempo 30 und Tempo 50 in deutschen Städten: Nützlicher Flickenteppich
spiegel.description: Mal Tempo 30, mal Tempo 50: Der Flickenteppich an Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzungen in deutschen Städten nervt viele Autofahrer. Doch eine Studie legt nahe, dass der Wirrwarr sogar hilft.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Im Kink-Club KitKat galt Diskretion. Nun erscheinen gleich zwei Dokus. Was erzählen sie über unser Sexleben?
News: Xi Jinping bei Donald Trump, Herbstgutachten wohl positiv, Unfallrückgang bei Tempo 30
spiegel.description: Xi und Trump reden über künstliche Intelligenz. Die Wirtschaftsinstitute haben wohl gute Nachrichten. Und Tempo-30-Schilder wirken anders, als Sie vielleicht denken. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: USS »Abraham Lincoln«: Pentagon räumt Suizidversuche von Crewmitgliedern ein
spiegel.description: Monatelang hatten Donald Trump und das Pentagon die katastrophalen Zustände an Bord der USS »Abraham Lincoln« kleingeredet. Nun räumen die US-Streitkräfte ein: Mehrere Crewmitglieder haben versucht, sich das Leben zu nehmen.

spiegel.title: OpenAI: KI-Agent hackt sich eigenständig in australische Regierungswebsite
spiegel.description: Australiens Premier spricht von einem »inakzeptablen« Vorfall: Ein KI-Agent hat sich unbefugt Zugriff auf Behördendaten verschafft. OpenAI meldete Canberra das erst drei Monate später – per E-Mail an ein allgemeines Postfach.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump empfängt Xi Jinping in den USA - und ein US-Bomber bringt ihn aus der Fassung
spiegel.description: Diese Szene dürfte als Meme weiterleben: Beim Empfang des chinesischen Präsidenten in den USA gehörte auch ein Überflug durch Kampfjets zum Programm. Donald Trump war auf deren Lautstärke ganz offensichtlich nicht vorbereitet.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump empfängt Xi Jinping in den USA - die Fotos
spiegel.description: Chinas Staatspräsident ist in den USA angekommen, zum ersten Mal seit 2023. Begrüßt wurde Xi Jinping von Donald Trump persönlich. Die besten Bilder.

spiegel.title: Brasilien: Rekordhitze und El Niño verschärfen Feuerkrise in Manaus
spiegel.description: Zahlreiche Brände haben die Amazonas-Metropole Manaus in dichten Rauch gehüllt. Im Vergleich zum Vorjahr ist die Zahl der Feuer um mehr als 300 Prozent gestiegen – auch wegen des Klimaphänomens El Niño.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Wolodymyr Selenskyj bezeichnet Putin als »Patient null« der Kriegstreiberei
spiegel.description: Der Präsident der Ukraine hat vor der Uno-Vollversammlung erneut um Unterstützung geworben. Selenskyj betonte dabei nicht nur die Sicherheit seines eigenen Landes: Putin sei als »Patient null« eine noch größere Gefahr.

spiegel.title: Chefs von Anthropic und OpenAI warnen vor KI-Gefahren »für die gesamte Menschheit«
spiegel.description: KI-Unternehmer Dario Amodei und Sam Altman haben den Uno-Sicherheitsrat davor gewarnt, dass schlecht verwaltete KI die Menschheit bedrohen könne. Erst einen Tag zuvor haben beide günstigere KI-Modelle veröffentlicht.

spiegel.title: Wahlkommission in Israel stimmt für Ausschluss arabischer Parteien
spiegel.description: In etwa einem Monat treten die Bürgerinnen und Bürger in Israel an die Wahlurne. Jetzt wird wohl das Oberste Gericht entscheiden müssen, ob die größten Parteien der arabischen Minderheit zur Wahl stehen.

spiegel.title: BER stellte Flugbetrieb wegen Drohnensichtung kurzzeitig ein
spiegel.description: Am Hauptstadtflughafen BER ist am Abend eine Drohne gesichtet worden. Flüge wurden für eine Dreiviertelstunde eingestellt, inzwischen dürfen Flugzeuge wieder starten und landen.

spiegel.title: Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang und Donald Trump: Der KI-Einflüsterer
spiegel.description: Jensen Huang leitet Nvidia, das wertvollste Unternehmen der Welt. Von KI-Horrorszenarien hält er nichts – so ist er zum wichtigen Verbündeten von Donald Trump geworden. Doch hinter der Bromance steckt noch mehr.

nyt.title: As Xi Visits Washington, Trump Plays Down China’s Actions Against U.S. Interests
nyt.description: Despite the rivalry between the United States and China, President Trump has repeatedly found ways to give President Xi Jinping of China a pass, portraying him more as a personal friend than a competitor.

nyt.title: U.S. and China Agree to Extend Trade Truce by 2 Months, Bessent Says
nyt.description: The Treasury secretary, who is leading talks with China, said the countries had agreed to extend a trade truce until January.

nyt.title: As Trump Welcomes Xi, More Americans Have a Positive View of China
nyt.description: Experts attribute the changing mood to fading memories of the coronavirus pandemic, awareness of China’s tech innovations and disaffection with President Trump’s trade wars.

nyt.title: From a Nepal in Pain, a Young Leader Makes a Case for Climate Reparations
nyt.description: Balendra Shah, 36, comes to the U.N. as a sun-glassed symbol of Gen Z political power. But concerns about his style are growing at home after devastating floods left thousands dead or missing.

nyt.title: Trump Invites Putin to Attend Group of 20 Summit in Miami
nyt.description: Many leaders are unlikely to welcome the Russian leader’s presence at the event because of his country’s war against Ukraine.

nyt.title: Trump Aides Seek to Jump Start Diplomacy With Iran as Crisis Widens
nyt.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that U.S. negotiators had restarted conversations about Iran’s nuclear program, but that there were no breakthroughs.

nyt.title: Mary Peltola’s Campaign in Alaska Senate Race Is Rocked by Tumult, With Angry Outbursts and Slurs
nyt.description: Democrats hope that Mary Peltola can flip a Republican Senate seat in Alaska. Former aides describe a campaign and congressional office marked by chaos.

nyt.title: Timothy Mellon, a G.O.P. Billionaire, Pulls Back His Money From Senate Republicans
nyt.description: Timothy Mellon, one of the party’s biggest donors in 2024, has so far withheld his midterm donations for Republican senators because he is unhappy about the failure to pass a key Trump priority.

nyt.title: Judge Holds Off on Immediate Ruling on White House’s Media Ban
nyt.description: Judge Timothy J. Kelly heard arguments about President Trump’s recent decision to bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House grounds. He said he would issue a decision about it “as soon as possible.”

nyt.title: Iowa Judge Dismisses Trump’s Lawsuit Against The Des Moines Register
nyt.description: The suit challenged a poll that showed Trump trailing Kamala Harris in the final weeks of the 2024 race. A judge warned that similar legal challenges could have a chilling effect on news reporting.

nyt.title: Mark Carney Interview: Canada’s Leader Lays Out Vision for Breaking Reliance on U.S.
nyt.description: In a wide-ranging interview, the Canadian leader laid out a detailed vision for breaking his country’s dependency on the United States.

nyt.title: Trump’s New Favorite Neighbor: Mexico
nyt.description: President Trump built his political brand in part on bashing Mexico. Now his second presidency depends on deepening partnerships with the country.

nyt.title: 8 Sailors in U.S.S. Lincoln Strike Group Attempted Suicide, Navy Says
nyt.description: The aircraft carrier with its crew of about 5,000 sailors has spent more than 300 days at sea.

nyt.title: OpenAI’s A.I. Tried Breaching Four Other Targets, With No Prompting
nyt.description: In each incident, the technology appeared to be conducting mundane data collection and resorted to hacking techniques to get it, researchers said.

nyt.title: Australia Says OpenAI ‘Infiltrated’ Public Health Care Portal
nyt.description: Australia is exploring potential legal action after an artificial intelligence agent accessed nonpublic information on the country’s universal health care system.

nyt.title: A Powerful Nor’easter Is Taking Shape. How It Could Affect Your Forecast.
nyt.description: The forecast for this weekend became a lot clearer on Wednesday, but meteorologists warned that the storm’s exact path was still uncertain.

nyt.title: Melania Trump’s Busy Schedule: A New Show, a Foster-Care Bill and Reading Executive Orders
nyt.description: In a burst of activity this week, the enigmatic first lady told Americans what she has been up to after a quiet summer. Her activities have included filming a new documentary series about her life.

nyt.title: The U.S. and China Are Far Apart on A.I. Safety
nyt.description: Beijing and Washington may use the same language of A.I. safety, but they are trying to protect very different things.

npr.title: OpenAI's breach of Australian health department website prompts rebuke
npr.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he was extremely concerned about OpenAI 's breach of an Australian health department website that the artificial intelligence company took too long to reveal.

npr.title: Fears of return to war grow in Ethiopia's Tigray region
npr.description: Fears are growing of a return to war in Ethiopia's Tigray region, just four years after a devastating conflict ended in a fragile peace deal.

npr.title: Here's what happened on day 2 of the UN General Assembly
npr.description: Iran and Ukraine take center stage at the UN as diplomats push to contain two wars threatening global stability.

npr.title: Does the UN have a future?
npr.description: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Susan Rice about the relevance of the United Nations in 2026.

npr.title: Trump and Xi meet at moment of global consequence
npr.description: It is the second time the leaders are meeting this year after the Beijing summit in May.

npr.title: Iran's president gives a rare wartime speech at the U.N.
npr.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the U.N. General Assembly a day after President Trump threatened from the same podium to "annihilate" Iran.

npr.title: From cybersecurity to AI to Taiwan, what's at stake in Trump's summit with Xi
npr.description: As President Trump and China's President Xi prepare to meet, Rush Doshi of the Council on Foreign Relations explains the current state of U.S.-China relations and what to expect from this summit.

npr.title: Greetings from Edinburgh, where a cheeky tour guide makes art history hilarious
npr.description: For anyone who grew up staring blankly at museum artwork, this is the fun that was missing: Coco leads interactive and (mostly) factual art history comedy tours.

npr.title: Is Nepal's flood a harbinger of what's to come in the Himalayas?
npr.description: Building dams and hydropower plants in the Himalayas holds great promise for providing electricity. In the wake of the Nepal disaster, experts are asking about the risks of such construction.

npr.title: Dems have an edge over GOP, poll finds. And, ICE looks into 'mobile detention centers'
npr.description: An NPR poll shows that Democrats have an edge over Republicans going into the midterms, partially due to Trump. And, Immigration and Customs Enforcement is looking into "mobile detention centers."

elpais.title: Sánchez carga contra Ayuso y Almeida por la “tragedia social” del desahucio de Maricarmen: “Están más preocupados en comprar aticazos”
elpais.description: El presidente dice que no “descarta nada” para impedir los desahucios pero admite que necesita a sus socios, que han rechazado ya dos veces el escudo

elpais.title: El símbolo de un derecho roto
elpais.description: Maricarmen Abascal, desahuciada a los 87 años por un fondo de inversión, pone rostro y nombre al drama de la vivienda en España

elpais.title: Maricarmen, de 87 años, es desahuciada de su casa y se irá temporalmente con unos familiares
elpais.description: La vecina de Retiro ha rechazado la plaza de emergencia gratuita en una residencia que le ofrecía el Ayuntamiento de Madrid

elpais.title: El desahucio de Maricarmen provoca una conmoción social y política
elpais.description: Miles de personas cortan las calles de Madrid en una manifestación espontánea que comenzó frente al ático que compró la Comunidad de Madrid en Chamberí

elpais.title: Por qué pudieron desahuciar a Maricarmen
elpais.description: A sus 87 años, ha sido expulsada del piso de Madrid en el que vivía desde 1956. Su caso plantea hasta dónde llega la protección legal de los inquilinos vulnerables

elpais.title: Hasta luego, Maricarmen
elpais.description: La mujer de 87 años fue sacada en camilla, como una víctima de guerra, pero cada día se ejecutan desahucios en barrios menos fotogénicos sin que se nos mueva una ceja

elpais.title: Dirigentes del PSOE lamentan las “contradicciones” de Zapatero con las joyas: “¿Dónde queda la ética?”
elpais.description: Cargos socialistas se declaran “desolados” por el regalo realizado por “una monarquía medieval que no respeta los derechos humanos” como Arabia Saudí mientras Ferraz mantiene la confianza en la inocencia del expresidente

elpais.title: El valor de las joyas de Zapatero según la tasación pericial apunta a un delito fiscal, aunque haya prescrito
elpais.description: El expresidente trata de desvincular el “obsequio” de su condición de jefe del Ejecutivo, pese a que recibió las piezas durante un viaje oficial del rey saudí a España

elpais.title: Sánchez, en la ONU: “Ceuta saldrá de la crisis sin convertir al inmigrante en un enemigo, respetando derechos humanos”
elpais.description: El presidente lanza en su último viaje a Nueva York antes de las elecciones su discurso más anti Trump y llama al optimismo de los progresistas

elpais.title: Delcy Rodríguez agradece a Trump su papel en Venezuela y asegura que habrá elecciones sin concretar la fecha
elpais.description: La presidenta vuelve a la Asamblea General, foro en el que arremetió contra EE UU, sin mencionar a Maduro, encarcelado a tan solo 14 kilómetros de la sede de la ONU

elpais.title: Alfombra roja, flores y Trump: así ha sido la llegada de Xi Jinping a Washington
elpais.description: Los líderes de EE UU y China se reúnen este jueves para tratar sobre comercio, inteligencia artificial, Taiwán y la guerra en Irán, entre otros asuntos

elpais.title: Ariana Harwicz, escritora excluida del Cultur Alh: “En la cultura se justifica la cancelación a los judíos”
elpais.description: La autora argentina, cuya participación en el festival granadino fue anulada, lamenta que “escritoras feministas” la señalaran y “que haya sido un hombre, Banville”, quien se solidarizara con ella

elpais.title: El último acto de lealtad de ‘Lur’, el perro que delató al asesino de su dueño gracias a que tenía chip
elpais.description: La identificación de un perro fue clave para reconocer unos restos hallados en un embalse de Zaragoza y llegar hasta su homicida, que acabó con él por problemas en la convivencia

elpais.title: Raúl Arévalo: “He trabajado con algún director que hoy sería denunciado. Seguro que ahora no se comportaría así”
elpais.description: Hace 20 años estrenó ‘azuloscurocasinegro’ y hoy, a sus 46, es un virtuoso. Ahora, tras el éxito de ‘El ser querido’, el actor madrileño interpreta a un gran villano en la serie ‘El castillo’

elpais.title: ¿Una hogaza de pan a 60 dólares? Analizamos el fenómeno viral con quienes se dedican al oficio
elpais.description: La recién inaugurada panadería Rye en Nueva York, que solo vende pan de centeno, se ha viralizado por el elevado precio de su hogaza, convertida en diana de críticas para unos y en objeto de deseo para otros

elpais.title: Los hombres que caminan por delante de sus parejas: por qué esos pasos por delante sí importan
elpais.description: La manera en la que las parejas caminan juntas revela mucho acerca de las relaciones de poder existentes en ellas

elpais.title: Los ‘ricos’, según Irene Montero
elpais.description: La eurodiputada de Podemos utiliza un trampantojo que exculpa a la clase política de no saber resolver los problemas de la ciudadanía

elpais.title: Ese libro está muy bien, pero no me acuerdo de nada
elpais.description: Olvidar las novelas y ensayos que leemos resulta habitual y, dependiendo del texto, hasta sano

lanacion.title: Javier Milei y sus medidas, EN VIVO: el mandatario habló en la ONU y aseguró que el peronismo propone un “cuento de hadas”
lanacion.description: El minuto a minuto de las decisiones del Presidente, las reacciones de la oposición y las declaraciones de los funcionarios

lanacion.title: La Anmat prohibió la venta de un fármaco para tratar la diabetes por representar un “riesgo para la salud”
lanacion.description: El organismo alertó que el componente “retatrutide” se encuentra en etapa de investigación clínica por sus potenciales efectos

lanacion.title: Hacían tareas de mantenimiento y le pasaron la cortadora de césped por encima: “Lo rescatamos en shock”
Javier Milei cierra su viaje a Nueva York: disertación en un club económico y reunión con Netanyahu
lanacion.description: El Presidente expondrá en una institución que reúne a referentes empresariales y financieros; por la tarde tendrá un encuentro con el premier israelí y luego emprenderá el regreso al país

lanacion.title: El discurso completo de Javier Milei, en la ONU: un drástico giro malvinero y el intento de ser el mejor soldado de las batallas trumpistas
lanacion.description: El Presidente hizo una defensa de la soberanía argentina de las islas, tema que apenas había tocado en los años previos; rechazó regular a la IA y acusó a Naciones Unidas de ser una “organización inútil”

lanacion.title: La selección se reconstruye sin Messi: baja el promedio de edad y aparecen variantes en puestos clave
lanacion.description: Tras el adiós de Messi y Otamendi, y con otros referentes en duda, la renovación ya se siente: dónde los piensa Scaloni

lanacion.title: Senado: el oficialismo aceptó cambios y la reforma del Banco Central deberá volver a Diputados
lanacion.description: El proyecto será tratado este jueves y se modificarán las mayorías para designar y remover a los directores; también se discutirán los cambios a la ley de zonas frías; la cena de Karina Milei con los senadores de LLA

lanacion.title: Juegos Suramericanos: una atleta argentina ganó el oro con una remontada y agradeció a quienes la ayudaron con una rifa
lanacion.description: Micaela Levaggi se impuso en los 1500 metros y recordó el apoyo económico que le brindaron muchas personas; en los últimos metros de la carrera logró pasar del quinto al primer puesto

lanacion.title: Rossano, el pueblo italiano de donde vienen los Mileo, el apellido original de los ancestros de Milei
lanacion.description: En esta ciudad de la Calabria jónica nació en 1918 Francesco Mileo, el abuelo de Javier Milei. Allí se casaron sus padres y allí comenzó a aparecer, en los documentos de sus descendientes, una alternancia entre Mileo y Milei que terminaría consolidándose en la Argentina.

lanacion.title: La formación de futuros profesionales, ¿en manos de la inteligencia artificial?
La agenda de la TV del jueves: la Fórmula 1 arranca en Bakú, los Suramericanos y empieza la Nations League europea
lanacion.description: La actividad deportiva en la continuidad de la semana, disponible a través de las pantallas

lanacion.title: Juezas abolicionistas desenmascaradas
lanacion.description: Las decisiones de dos magistradas contra la ley que bajó la edad de imputabilidad penal desatienden a las víctimas y protegen a los delincuentes

lanacion.title: Rusia puso retenciones cero para el trigo, la cebada y el maíz hasta fin de año
lanacion.description: La medida había sido anticipada a comienzos de septiembre y quedó formalizada por un decreto firmado por el primer ministro Mijaíl Mishustin; rige con efecto retroactivo desde el 1° de septiembre hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2026, en un contexto de dificultades logísticas y presión sobre los precios internos

lanacion.title: El Pro criticó la política de discapacidad del Gobierno: “Debe ser abordada con previsión, responsabilidad y respuestas”

undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain

Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

proj-syn.title: How Trade Deals Can Save Nature
proj-syn.description: Environmental conservation is among the most important, universally shared imperatives the world faces, and market access is one of the few carrots available in international politics. By linking tariffs to deforestation, the EU and others can create trade agreements that deliver more conservation and more gains from trade.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Third Way on China
proj-syn.description: Instead of choosing between a confrontation with China and business as usual, European policymakers should examine the benefits and costs of trade sector by sector to identify where mutually beneficial arrangements remain possible. Economic modeling shows that pragmatism beats more extreme options in most cases.

proj-syn.title: Alarm Bells in the Balkans
proj-syn.description: Recent developments in the Balkans ought to be a wake-up call for Europe, given the potential for nationalist provocations in one country to spill over within the region. Multiple elections coming next month raise the risk of a dangerous descent into political instability.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s 21st-Century Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Since his return to the White House, Donald Trump has turned his back on the free-market principles that the United States spent decades championing. In doing so, he threatens to dismantle the economic order that helped produce unprecedented growth in global output and trade.

proj-syn.title: The AI Productivity Delusion
proj-syn.description: As with previous technological revolutions, it is natural to focus on AI's net effects: Will it create more than it destroys? But unlike previous eras of creative destruction, the real question this time is, “Create more of what?”

proj-syn.title: Technological Leapfrogging in the AI Age
proj-syn.description: Across Africa, past success stories have led policymakers to believe that developing economies can usually bypass the arduous, expensive stages of infrastructure development by adopting technologies built elsewhere. But this approach deserves more scrutiny, especially when applied to imported AI systems.

proj-syn.title: Preventing an AI World War
proj-syn.description: Warnings that AI may lead to our extinction often overlook the most immediate risk: a war triggered by an attack that no human intended or approved. A mechanism for distinguishing unintended harm from deliberate attacks is urgently needed.

proj-syn.title: Post-Liberal Europe?
proj-syn.description: Another victory for the far right in a German state election has confirmed European liberals' worst fears. With many critical European elections approaching in 2027, debates about the proper limits of popular sovereignty and other fundamental tenets of liberalism are now of paramount importance.

proj-syn.title: Germany’s Moment of Reckoning
proj-syn.description: As its growth model runs out of road, Germany must decide whether to defend aging industries or enable new ones to emerge. To translate its research excellence into globally competitive companies, it needs deeper capital markets and a genuine European single market in which promising startups can grow.

proj-syn.title: Is Germany’s Firewall Collapsing?
proj-syn.description: After achieving an historic victory in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt earlier this month, the far-right Alternative für Deutschland has just finished first in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, too. Do the results vindicate critics who argue that uniting to keep the AfD out of power is undemocratic and ultimately self-defeating?

proj-syn.title: The Middle Powers Are Now the “Free World”
proj-syn.description: Europe, Canada, and the democracies of Africa, Asia, and Latin America now bear the burden of keeping the old American ideal of the free world alive. While the ideal was always a noble lie, it enabled hundreds of millions of people to imagine a better world during the Cold War, and it could do so again.

proj-syn.title: What Xi Really Wants From Trump
proj-syn.description: As US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, prepare to meet in Washington, American policymakers must not underestimate China’s ambitions. Under Xi, its foreign policy is focused on securing the support of the Global South while pursuing the long-term goal of seizing Taiwan and achieving global preeminence.

proj-syn.title: Europe in a Multi-Aligned World
proj-syn.description: As the Sino-American rivalry intensifies, Europe may be tempted to position itself as a third pole of geopolitics. But instead of defining its power in relation to a bipolarity that many countries are seeking to escape, the continent should focus on building a new architecture of interdependence in which it occupies a central role.

proj-syn.title: A Central European Model for EU Growth
proj-syn.description: As the European Union struggles to revive growth and loses ground to the United States and China, its economic future looks increasingly uncertain. Central Europe’s experience suggests that reversing that decline will require fostering innovation while helping poorer countries catch up.

proj-syn.title: Might Makes Right Will End Pax Americana
proj-syn.description: Far from bolstering US dominance, Donald Trump’s embrace of coercive militarism has eroded it. When the distinction between war and peace dissolves into a ceasefire that is neither, and months of bombardment fail to deliver anything like victory, force looks less like strength and more like pointless destruction.

proj-syn.title: A Roadmap for the Next UN Secretary-General
proj-syn.description: The next UN secretary-general will take over the most prominent position in multilateral governance at a time when multilateralism is arguably at its nadir. Adapting to today’s multipolar reality will require instilling a renewed sense of purpose and demanding more of member states.

proj-syn.title: A New World Order Is Not Beckoning
proj-syn.description: It does no good to get misty-eyed about the demise of the liberal international “order.” What the world really needs to manage today's biggest risks is a different, more realistic narrative that does not draw a sharp line between a disintegrating ideal and its post-liberal successor.

proj-syn.title: What It Means for Global Warming to Exceed 1.5°C
proj-syn.description: A sobering new report from the United Nations Environment Programme warns that even if governments deliver on all their existing climate pledges, warming could reach 1.8°C later this century. That means humanity must pivot from simply containing global warming to finding ways to reverse it.

crunchbase.title: Jumbo-Sized Series A Rounds Are On The Rise
crunchbase.description: So far this year, global startups have secured at least 114 Series A rounds of $100 million or more, per Crunchbase data. That’s the highest annual total in years and on track to top the all-time peak. We take a look at where the money is going.

crunchbase.title: The Emerging M&A Map For AI Agent Security
crunchbase.description: As AI agents gain access to enterprise data, systems and tools, they are emerging as a new class of active identity requiring specialized permissions, monitoring and governance, writes guest author Itay Sagie. He believes the market, and its M&A opportunities, will likely form around specific control points, making precise positioning crucial for startups.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Can You Trust That AI Agent? Baselayer Raises $35M To Help Companies Decide

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Large Rounds For AI Infrastructure, Space Tech And Investment Management Lead
crunchbase.description: After a week of multiple billion-dollar-plus rounds, startup investors have reduced the number of zeroes on their funding checks. This past week, the largest U.S. startup funding rounds were in the hundreds of millions, topped by a $550 million financing for AI infrastructure company Temporal Technologies and a $308 million investment in space vehicle developer Impulse Space.

crunchbase.title: What 25,000 Startup Applications Reveal About The New Rules Of Seed-Stage Startups
crunchbase.description: The most-fundable startups prioritize a clear go-to-market strategy and test distinctive marketing channels early, treating distribution and disciplined focus as durable competitive advantages, explains guest author Aaron Golbin, a co-founder and general partner at LvlUp Ventures, who believes that seed-stage success depends on focused execution, diversified financing, built-in distribution, rapid learning and AI designed as core infrastructure.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Fintech Offers Startups Alternative To Venture Debt With A New Model To Finance Customer Acquisition Costs

crunchbase.description: From putting nuclear reactors on barges to grading how well AI models can control robots, this month’s crop of interesting startup deals takes AI and other emerging technologies well beyond the conventional software stack.
